newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm ministers agree citrus fruit aid programme.
newsitem.headline: Farm ministers agree citrus fruit aid programme.

text.p: European Union farm ministers agreed a Commission proposal which will give aid to citrus fruit farmers rather than processors, EU officials said.

Last minute amendments to a second Irish Presidency compromise mean that the proposal can now formally be adopted as an A point at a forthcoming Council of Ministers meeting even though Spain voted against the agreement.

A demand from Greece that the scheme should be extended to include 6,000 tonnes of grapefruit was accepted by ministers and Spain succeeded in raising the threshold for citrus fruit to 320,000 tonnes from the compromise proposal of 315,000 tonnes.
The European Commission told ministers that the new regime will provide flexibility while ensuring that all fruit on which aid is paid will be processed.
During lengthy negotiations, producer countries insisted that the calculation of quota overruns will be on a three year average.
The budgetary cost of the aid for citrus fruit and for the inclusion of grapefruit will be offset by a decrease in the orange threshhold to just under 1.2 million tonnes.
